items.name: Kajo Park (Yamagata Castle ruins)
items.body: The moated grounds of Yamagata Castle, free and open year-round, with several free history stops clustered inside — the Mogami Yoshiaki Historical Museum, the octagonal Meiji-era Kyu-Saiseikan, and the reconstructed Otemon Yagura gate-tower. The Yagura's interior is open to visitors, though stairs-only access isn't confirmed — worth checking ahead for anyone with limited mobility.

items.name: Bunshokan
items.kicker: Free · the most accessible culture stop in the city
items.body: The former prefectural capitol, a Taisho-era building with the best-documented step-free access of any Yamagata city sight — worth prioritizing for the group's 2 low-mobility travelers. The former assembly chamber was closed for construction, targeted to reopen by the end of September 2026 — re-check before counting on seeing it.

items.name: Kyu-Saiseikan
items.body: A distinctive octagonal, 3-tier former Meiji-era hospital building inside Kajo Park — free, and genuinely off the beaten path since most visitors head straight for the castle grounds instead.

items.name: Mogami Yoshiaki Historical Museum
items.body: Dedicated to the daimyo who actually built Yamagata Castle — small, free, and squarely on-theme for a culture/history-focused visit without appearing on generic top-10 lists.

items.name: Risshaku-ji (Yamadera)
items.body: A mountain temple complex climbing a cliff face above the Yamadera valley, reached by a direct Senzan Line train from Yamagata. Admission is {{fact:yamadera-admission-500-yen}}. No cable car or shortcut exists — the climb to the Godaido viewing platform is on foot, the whole way. Konponchudo, the main hall near the base, is a complete stop on its own for anyone who'd rather not attempt the stairs.

items.name: Ginzan Onsen
items.kicker: Gas-lit ryokan street · best before 11:00 or after evening lamp-lighting
items.body: A Taisho-era wooden ryokan street along the Ginzan River, gas lamps lighting ≈16:30-17:00 (seasonal — the schedule shifts earlier as sunset comes sooner through October), plus the riverside "Waraku" foot bath and Shirogane Falls (22m) at the street's end. Midday is the most crowded window; staying overnight pays off here — before roughly 7:00 the street is nearly empty, well ahead of the day-trip crowds.

items.name: Yamagata Marugoto-kan Beninokura
items.kicker: Free to browse · ≈10 min walk from the station
items.body: A restored Edo-era safflower (beniba) merchant's warehouse compound — genuinely local, easy walking distance from the station, and pairs naturally with lunch at Soba Sanbyakubou inside the same complex.

items.correction: Raised to ¥500 as of April 1, 2025 — many guides and aggregator sites still quote the old figure.

items.claim: A cable car or ropeway can take you partway up Yamadera.
items.correction: No mechanized assist exists anywhere on the mountain. The only way beyond the base is on foot, via roughly 1,015 stone steps.

items.claim: You can drive up and park in Ginzan Onsen itself.
items.correction: The town center is pedestrian-only regardless. Day-trip parking sits on Route 188 outside the village. A winter 2025-26 car/entry-ticket restriction ran through March 1, 2026, and a shorter autumn 2025 version ran just two November weekends — 2026 dates for either aren't announced yet, so re-check closer to the trip; route buses, delivery vehicles, and overnight guests' ryokan parking are exempt regardless.

items.claim: IC cards (Suica) work everywhere around Yamagata the way they do in Tokyo.
items.correction: Ōishida Station — the gateway to Ginzan Onsen — doesn't accept IC cards, and the bus onward is cash-only regardless. Carry cash for that whole leg.
